prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a sideswipe while changing lanes in Houston, Texas, and has whiplash. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1244; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not give my name on the recording, if that's all right. You can use the claim number.

Q: That's fine. Can you tell me where you were when the accident happened?
A: I was driving on a multi-lane highway in Houston, Texas, heading into the city during the afternoon commute.

Q: What were you doing right before the collision?
A: I was changing lanes to move over to the right. I checked my mirror and the lane looked clear, so I signaled and started to merge.

Q: Did you see the other vehicle at any point?
A: Not until it was right beside me. There was a loud scrape and my car jerked toward the shoulder. I think the other car was in my blind spot.

Q: Did either vehicle stop after contact?
A: Both of us pulled onto the shoulder. The other driver got out and we exchanged information.

Q: How are you feeling physically now?
A: My neck and upper back are stiff and sore. When I turn my head to check traffic, I get a sharp pain down into my shoulders. I also had a headache for a couple of days.

Q: Have you seen a doctor or other medical provider since the accident?
A: Yes, I went to an urgent care clinic that same day. They diagnosed whiplash and gave me a neck brace and some medication. I've been doing physical therapy twice a week since then.

Q: Are you still experiencing those symptoms?
A: Yes, they're better than they were, but I still have stiffness, especially in the morning, and I can't sit for long periods without discomfort.

Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?
A: Only that I was trying to be careful and I didn't expect a car to be there. I'm hoping the claim can be resolved so I can get my treatment covered.

Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
A: Thank you.
